chunks: Al-Hasan ibn Mahbub from Ibn Ri'ab said:

I asked Abu al-Hasan Musa (peace be upon him) about a man who was related to me, who died leaving young children and leaving slave boys and girls, and did not make a will. What do you think about the one who buys from them a girl and takes her as an Umm Walad (mother of a child), and what do you think about their sale? He said: 'If they have a guardian who manages their affairs, he sells on their behalf and looks after their interests, he is rewarded in doing so.' I said: 'What do you think about the one who buys from them a girl and takes her as an Umm Walad?' He said: 'There is no harm in that, if the guardian who manages their affairs sells on their behalf regarding what is beneficial for them, then they have no right to return/revoke what the guardian who manages their affairs regarding what is beneficial for them has done.'

key_terms.أُمَّ وَلَدٍ: Umm Walad (a female slave who bears a child to her master)

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on a guardian selling a young slave girl who becomes an Umm Walad?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Imam Musa al-Kazim (AS) clarifies the fiqh of guardianship (wilayah) over minor orphans, emphasizing that a guardian's sale of slave children is binding and irrevocable if done in their best interest (maslahah). This ruling underscores the practical authority of the wali in managing orphan assets, specifically regarding the status of 'Umm Walad' and the finality of such transactions when executed properly.
